## Typhoon 台風

_dedicated to my brother Tristan Skybreak_

Once I finish the full-sized painting of this:

1.  That painting is going to my brother Skybreak
2.  You'll see this appear as a proper feature on the site
3.  I will open up prints for sale

Until then, this remains my favorite of the three "natural disaster" fractal paintings that I created as a triptych in 2018. "Tsunami" remains a close second, but cannot match the depth and detail of "Typhoon" itself.

Sometimes the plans I make overstep my own bounds to accomplish them. It's a side-effect of continually aiming for the moon. In this case, the final piece that I want to create will be made with custom stamps that I cut out, then using different wood stains on top of a panel. I've already tested it out in smaller versions, and the concept is sound. It's the final piece though that still remains to be created.

And that is a test for another day.

The Natural Disaster Fractals on Instagram:

\[[Tsunami 津波 on IG](https://www.instagram.com/p/BMooi1Rlky8/)\] \[[Cyclone κύκλος on IG](https://www.instagram.com/p/BMolo0lFyeh/)\] \[[Typhoon 台風 on IG](https://www.instagram.com/p/BMojAx0l4QE/)\]

## Xu Bing's Square Word Calligraphy We temporarily interrupt this section with an important not-all-too disconnected segue. To the right, I've written the word "TYPHOON" in Xu Bing's incredible square word calligraphy script. My sister Gaea turned me on to Xu Bing this very year, here in 2026. As soon as I started testing it out myself, I knew it would be an organic and beautiful fit for my "natural disaster" series of Mandelbrot spirals, including the one you see here above. Then I dove into the rabbit hole, discovering more about Xu Bing himself. Xu Bing fucking GETS IT! Chairman Mao tore his family apart, throwing his father in a prison camp and shutting down the very art school he'd been attending (along with all the other ones). He saw scripts and words become more militaristic, more staccato... more dividing. Xu's first breakout piece of art was the "Book from the Sky", meticulously painted calligraphy that follows every rule of the Ancient Mandarin script... but... while following the rules, not a single symbol has ever been used. It haunts the mind of the viewer, because it SHOULD make sense, there SHOULD be meaning in these symbols... but they elude meaning. I'm really not doing him justice with these small words. BUT! Since you'll be seeing my use of square word calligraphy more and more in my art, I had to shout out this incredible artist! ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eoB6wRkOOxY)) _...now, to get back to shilling!_

## Benthic Saltlife Whoever you are, the one who buys a scarf with this design every few years, _I see you._ I just wish I knew you! You're somewhere in the UK. You've got great taste in scarves. That's as much as I know. For everyone else, "Saltlife" will always hold a special place in my heart as my very first sell that I ever made from my fractals. It was on Redbubble and it spurred me onward to open up other designs for sale. I love to swim. I love to feel like I'm floating, surrounded completely, and to explore an entirely different world. We share our planet with the ocean, yet it truly is as alien to the land and air... even more alien than was ever invented for any science fiction planet. \[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/21221666)\]

## Lantern Festival

_aka, "Chinese New Year"_

This is a technique used in exploring the Mandelbrot Set called "orbit trapping", where you isolate an iteration, then fold it in on itself in a perfect circle. It creates these beautiful, hypnotic tentacle-like structures at every level. Then fine-tuning your color palette lets you control the detailing and patterns formed by the structure.

I lit the design with some of my favorite colors to be experienced in this life, which is the lantern festivals held throughout Asia celebrating the passing of those we love from this current iteration of the simulation in which we inhabit.. . watching as the flames float down rivers and rise into the skies.. carrying them away from us.

\[[Lantern Festival on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/28383134)\]

## "Bloom of Lilacs"

_aka, "The Love of Lavender"_

This is actually one of my oldest professional designs. I was exploring "Elephant Valley" within the Mandelbrot and came upon an area that I could only call: "The Elephants Are On Parade". I began to work on the palette, and then the 3D depths of the fractal itself, until it seemed as if an entire spiral galaxy was emerging.

As with many of my most popular Mandelbrot fractals, there is an incredible amount of detail and the depth-effect lends itself to the appearance of tentacles. Being that I love both lavender and our tentacled octopi family that cohabit this planet alongside us, you'll hear no complaints from me.

From one side, it is a cloud of lilac and lavender petals swirling in the heart of a dust devil. From the other side, it is a cosmic white light explosion of galaxies formed around the eyes of elephants.

_There's no wrong way to look at it._

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/20965908)\]

## RGB I've been interested in a type of glitch processing called "color splitting" for more than a decade, a method that grew out of intentionally breaking VHS and cable signals so that the different color channels show through. I've since built it into my own custom image-editors so that I can split the spectrum however I might desire. In this case I did most of the work manually, building it into the palette itself that here has been molded onto the Mandelbrot Set near one of my favorite areas -- Elephant Valley. The majority of the gradient is a simple monochrome ascension from black to white, then I spiked equal intervals inside the palette with red, green, and blue touches. You might see some yellow inside of the image, but that is actually an illusion created whenever the colors come near to one another. The yellow isn't real. It's not there. _Tyler gone_. As with most things surrounding our senses, simply put: _your eyes are lying to you_. The only colors in the palette are gray and shades of red, blue, and green. The rest is the lie. \[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/28861748)\]

## Disc World

_aka, "O-Zone"; aka, "At the Car Wash"_

This one came out of a scrapped design that I was working on for my remix of "[The Grid](daft-punk-the-grid-remix)" by Daft Punk. In the end, for that Daft Punk cover art, I went with a different design that I'd made in Apophysis. I came back to this scrapped design a year later, reworking it on a brighter background with more emphasis on the feeling of bubbles. The discs never really went away, but you can now feel that nickname of "at the car wash" that has since become better known than its original title.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/34706131)\]

### Extended Exploration

Many of my Mandelbrot fractals appeared in my "[Spectral Iteration](spectral-iteration)" book, along with writings and musings about Gaston Julia and Benoit Mandelbrot. If you like these spiral designs, you'd definitely want to check out my "[Heart of the Rose](heart-of-the-rose)" mural or my "[Nocturne of Scorpio](nocturne-of-scorpio)" fractal painting. For the Mandelbrot itself, I created "[The Great Blue Mandelbrot](great-blue-mandelbrot)" in the style of a map that you can get lost in.
